description:
FOUND s473t6c (#1501 ROUND 10).

t/op/recurse.t's row 27 ("64K deep recursion - no output expected") dies with
`sb-kernel::binding-stack-exhausted: Binding stack exhausted`, which the run
baseline records in its sig column as `crash:`.

PCL binds at least one DYNAMIC variable per call frame (the caller stack, the
current package, *wantarray*), so the BINDING stack is the recursion limit --
not the control stack, which `tools/lib/PCLSbcl.pm` already sizes ($STACK_MB).
SBCL's binding stack is sized by `--binding-stack-size`, which PCLSbcl does not
set.

TWO DIRECTIONS, and the first one is a one-line experiment: raise the binding
stack in the ONE command-line builder (PCLSbcl.pm, so every runner gets it) and
measure both the depth reached and the RSS cost.  The better answer is to stop
binding per frame -- the caller stack is the one that grows without bound -- but
that is the #233 caller-fidelity design, not a filler.

Do NOT "fix" this by catching the condition: the row asserts the program
SURVIVES the recursion, so swallowing the exhaustion still fails it.


=== MEASURED s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20): the limit is ~10k, not 64k, and it is NOT trappable ===
~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/probes/depth.pl: `sub down { my $n = shift; $n ? 1 + down($n-1) : 0 }` -- depth 8000 ok, depth 12000 = SBCL "Binding stack exhausted", the PROCESS dies (an enclosing `eval {}` does not catch it; perl runs 100k+).  An anonymous recursive closure dies below 5000 (scaling battery, last row).  #2083 (Math::BigFloat bdiv) is probably this limit and not an infinite recursion -- re-measure it with the depth printed.  The binding stack in SBCL is a build-time constant (1 MB); the lever on the PCL side is how many SPECIALS a p-sub call binds per frame (each binding = 16 bytes; ~10 per call at the measured limit).


=== THE LOOK OF IT (s494, Fable, Q5 failure-experience battery) ===
`sub r { my $n = shift; return $n == 0 ? 0 : 1 + r($n - 1) } print r(50000)` under `pcl`: perl prints 50000; pcl prints **1012 lines** on stderr starting `INFO: Binding stack guard page unprotected`, exit 1.  Whatever the depth fix is, the failure itself should be ONE line (perl`s own spelling for the nearest case is `Deep recursion on subroutine "%s"` as a WARNING, and then it keeps going) -- see #2108 for the uncaught-error shape.
subject: 64K-deep recursion exhausts SBCL's BINDING stack where perl runs it (op/recurse.t row 27; the runner records crash:)
